title: ‘Modern Love’: To Share or Not To Share? How Location Sharing Is Changing Our Relationships

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在早上4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能几乎每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用一个不同的首字母单词。

And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一个锅的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝成立175周年，陪伴您理解世界，充分过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，访问 nytimes.com 拼写斜杠 subscribe 获取特别优惠。

sentences.en: Love now and all.
sentences.zh: 爱现在以及一切。

sentences.en: You fall in love last time I love you.
sentences.zh: 上次我说爱你时，你坠入爱河。

sentences.en: Love is stronger than anything else.
sentences.zh: 爱比其他任何东西都强大。

sentences.en: I feel a love.
sentences.zh: 我感受到了一种爱。

sentences.en: And I love you more than anything.
sentences.zh: 我爱你胜过一切。

sentences.en: There's still love.
sentences.zh: 爱依然存在。

sentences.en: Love.
sentences.zh: 爱。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Anna Martin.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是安娜·马丁。

sentences.en: This is Modern Love.
sentences.zh: 这是《现代爱情》。

sentences.en: Our show is inspired by the Modern Love column and by all the messiness of trying to love, trust, and stay connected to other people.
sentences.zh: 我们的节目灵感来源于“现代爱情”专栏，以及试图去爱、去信任、去与他人保持联系时所经历的种种纷繁复杂。

sentences.en: One way my dad likes to stay connected is with a ritual he does basically every night.
sentences.zh: 我父亲喜欢保持联系的一种方式，是通过他基本上每晚都会做的一个仪式。

sentences.en: Before bed, he pulls out his phone, fires up the Find My Friends app, and sees that me and my two sisters are at home in our apartments.
sentences.zh: 睡觉前，他掏出手机，打开“查找我的朋友”应用，看我和两个妹妹是不是都在各自的公寓里。

sentences.en: And when he sees that, he sends a text to the family group chat that says something like,
sentences.zh: 当他看到这些时，他会在家庭群聊里发一条消息，内容大概是：

sentences.en: Ah, my three little chickadees at home in their nests.
sentences.zh: 啊，我的三个小山雀在各自的窝里呢。

sentences.en: It's simple.
sentences.zh: 很简单。

sentences.en: It's sweet.
sentences.zh: 很温馨。

sentences.en: It's a way he expresses his love.
sentences.zh: 这是他表达爱的一种方式。

sentences.en: And it's made possible by location sharing.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都是通过位置共享实现的。

sentences.en: We recently asked you to tell us how location sharing affects your relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们最近请大家告诉我们，位置共享是如何影响你们的人际关系的。

sentences.en: And you filled our inbox with stories about the people you're sharing your location with and the people you're not.
sentences.zh: 你们的收件箱里塞满了各种故事，关于那些你们与之共享位置的人，以及那些没有共享的人。

sentences.en: I share my location with a bunch of my friends and my parents and my brother.
sentences.zh: 我跟我的很多朋友、我父母还有我弟弟共享位置。

sentences.en: We've been together for about three years.
sentences.zh: 我们在一起大约三年了。

sentences.en: We've shared locations since the start.
sentences.zh: 从一开始我们就共享了位置。

sentences.en: My ex-husband and I are still sharing location.
sentences.zh: 我和我的前夫现在还在共享位置。

sentences.en: My children are out and about at night and we're trying to see where they are late.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子们晚上在外面到处跑，我们想看看他们深夜在哪里。

sentences.en: If they're past curfew, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果他们过了宵禁时间。

sentences.en: At first I didn't even want to do it because I just kind of felt icky about it.
sentences.zh: 起初我甚至不想这么做，因为我对它总觉得有点怪怪的、不舒服。

sentences.en: Right now I don't need to know where my girlfriend is 24-7.
sentences.zh: 现在我不需要全天候24小时都知道我女朋友在哪里。

sentences.en: I'm happy that we were sharing location services because I got to find out very early that he was cheating on me.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们开启了定位服务，因为我很早就发现他在背叛我。

sentences.en: He is getting married in two days and still shares his location with his ex-girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 他两天后就要结婚了，却仍然和他的前女友共享位置。

sentences.en: Because why not?
sentences.zh: 因为为什么不呢？

sentences.en: What is there to hide?
sentences.zh: 有什么好隐瞒的？

sentences.en: Your experiences with location sharing were, there's kind of no other way to put this, all over the map.
sentences.zh: 你们对位置共享的体验——说实话，真是不一而足。

sentences.en: A handful of you absolutely, unequivocally refuse to share your location with anyone, anywhere, ever.
sentences.zh: 你们中有少数人绝对、毫不含糊地拒绝与任何人、在任何地方、在任何时候共享位置。

sentences.en: But a lot of you said it adds something really valuable to your lives.
sentences.zh: 但你们中的很多人说，它给你们的生活增添了非常有价值的东西。

sentences.en: On multiple occasions my mother has called me to say, I'm loSt.
sentences.zh: 我母亲曾多次打电话给我说，我迷路了。

sentences.en: How do I get to wherever it is she was going?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么去她要去的地方？

sentences.en: And I could look at her location and tell her how to get there.
sentences.zh: 我可以看她的位置然后告诉她怎么走。

sentences.en: She loves the feeling of being taken care of that she gets from having me watch her, which is the exact opposite of how my adult children feel about sharing their location with me.
sentences.zh: 她很享受被我关注时那种被照顾的感觉，这与我的成年子女对与我共享位置的感受截然相反。

sentences.en: My brother David has Down syndrome.
sentences.zh: 我弟弟大卫患有唐氏综合征。

sentences.en: And when I see him, every once in a while he'll just like open up his phone and he'll show that both of us are in the same place.
sentences.zh: 当我见到他时，偶尔他会打开手机，展示我们俩都在同一个地方。

sentences.en: And he'll just burst out in happiness.
sentences.zh: 然后他就会高兴得合不拢嘴。

sentences.en: Probably about 45 minutes or so into the hike, I realized I was pretty loSt.
sentences.zh: 大概徒步了45分钟左右，我发现自己彻底迷路了。

sentences.en: I couldn't make heads or tails of the map that I had.
sentences.zh: 我完全看不懂我手里的地图。

sentences.en: So I ended up calling my partner.
sentences.zh: 所以我最后只好给我的伴侣打电话。

sentences.en: He was actually able to locate me on the map.
sentences.zh: 他竟然真的在地图上找到了我的位置。

sentences.en: I was so, so grateful that we had the tracking device available to us because I don't think I would have found my way back.
sentences.zh: 我非常非常感激我们有这个追踪设备可用，因为我觉得自己根本找不回去了。

sentences.en: So I would recommend it for couples who may be directionally challenged like myself.
sentences.zh: 所以我向那些可能像我一样方向感不佳的情侣推荐它。

sentences.en: On the flip side of that, there were stories like this next one, where location sharing started off okay, but took a bad turn.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，也有像接下来这个故事一样的情况，位置共享开始时还好，但后来却朝着不好的方向发展。

sentences.en: I moved to a new, much larger city, so I was a little nervous about being away from my hometown for really the first time,
sentences.zh: 我搬到了一座新的、大得多的城市，所以我有点紧张，这毕竟是我第一次离开家乡，

sentences.en: away from all the people who would typically know where I should be and if something terrible happened to me.
sentences.zh: 离开那些通常知道我在哪儿、如果我发生什么可怕的事能知道的人。

sentences.en: So it was a relief to make two really good girlfriends and all agreed to just share our locations with one another.
sentences.zh: 所以能结交两个非常好的女朋友，并且都同意互相共享位置，这让我松了一口气。

sentences.en: But it definitely ended up feeding into one of the friends, just insecurity, jealousy, the fact that she could always check our locations.
sentences.zh: 但它最终确实助长了其中一个朋友的不安全感、嫉妒心，因为她随时都能查看我们的位置。

sentences.en: She started just obsessively checking our locations and we'd get a text.
sentences.zh: 她开始强迫症般地查看我们的位置，然后我们就会收到一条短信。

sentences.en: Hey, didn't realize y'all were hanging out tonight.
sentences.zh: 嘿，没意识到你们今晚出来玩了。

sentences.en: Why didn't you invite me?
sentences.zh: 为什么不邀请我？

sentences.en: Or, hey, I see you're at my favorite coffee shop.
sentences.zh: 或者，嘿，我看到你在我最喜欢的咖啡馆。

sentences.en: Would have loved an invite.
sentences.zh: 要是有个邀请就好了。

sentences.en: So I had to end the friendship basically over that.
sentences.zh: 所以我基本上为了这件事不得不结束了这段友谊。

sentences.en: Being able to see someone's location is almost like having a superpower.
sentences.zh: 能够看到某人的位置几乎就像拥有超能力一样。

sentences.en: But like any superpower, it must be used responsibly.
sentences.zh: 但就像任何超能力一样，它必须负责任地使用。

sentences.en: And sometimes that means just turning it off.
sentences.zh: 有时这意味着把它关掉。

sentences.en: The relationship kind of ended on uncertain terMs.
sentences.zh: 这段关系在不确定的状态下结束了。

sentences.en: And in this uncertain period of kind of breakup, kind of not, I started very obsessively checking her location at all hours.
sentences.zh: 在这个处于分手边缘、又好像没有分手的动荡时期，我开始在全天候强迫症般地查看她的位置。

sentences.en: We're on a college campus in a very kind of contained radius.
sentences.zh: 我们在一个非常有限的大学校园半径范围内。

sentences.en: And it started turning into like not just like psychological anxiety, but like a physical manifestation.
sentences.zh: 这开始演变成不仅仅是心理焦虑，而是一种身体上的病症。

sentences.en: Like I just would not feel comfortable around her or even anywhere because I knew exactly where she was.
sentences.zh: 比如我在她身边或者甚至在任何地方都觉得很不自在，因为我确切地知道她在哪里。

sentences.en: And one night I was walking alone on the street and it was dusk and I had my headphones in and was listening to some sort of melodramatic music.
sentences.zh: 有一天晚上，我独自走在街上，当时天色昏暗，我塞着耳机，听着某种伤春悲秋的音乐。

sentences.en: And opened my phone and looked at her location and all of a sudden there was just kind of a snap of like, I need to stop.
sentences.zh: 我打开手机看了看她的位置，突然有一种瞬间清醒的感觉：我必须停下来。

sentences.en: I want to feel free.
sentences.zh: 我想感到自由。

sentences.en: It's clear that location sharing has changed something fundamental about our relationships.
sentences.zh: 很明显，位置共享已经改变了我们人际关系中某些根本的东西。

sentences.en: Whether you opt in, whether you opt out, someone in your life is probably going to feel some type of way about it.
sentences.zh: 无论你选择加入还是退出，你生活中的某个人大概都会对此有些情绪。

sentences.en: And everyone seems to need their own roadmap for where to draw the line.
sentences.zh: 而且每个人似乎都需要制定自己的路线图，来决定界限划在哪里。

sentences.en: Today on the show, I talk to a modern love essayist who has wrestled deeply with drawing his personal line around location sharing.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目中，我采访了一位《现代爱情》的专栏作家，他曾就如何划定自己关于位置共享的个人界限进行过深刻的挣扎。

sentences.en: And he tells me how a family tragedy made the stakes of that decision feel exceptionally high.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，一场家庭悲剧是如何让那个决定的利害关系变得异常重大的。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘文.

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的一个益智谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都创作《拼字蜂》和《字母箱》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色彩联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的人这样的一群人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 拼写斜杠 games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: When Arlen J.
sentences.zh: 当阿伦·J·

sentences.en: Staggs was a little kid, he had a lot of room to wander.
sentences.zh: 斯塔格斯还是个小孩子时，他有很多四处游荡的空间。

sentences.en: Whatever you picture of a boy growing up in rural Alabama, that's exactly what it looked like in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 无论你脑海中对80年代在阿拉巴马州乡村长大的男孩有什么印象，那里的景象就跟那完全一样。

sentences.en: There were all of these trails through the woods and creeks, and our parents never knew where we were.
sentences.zh: 树林和小溪里到处都是这样的小径，我们的父母从来不知道我们在哪儿。

sentences.en: Arlen was the youngest of three boys.
sentences.zh: 阿伦是三个男孩中最小的一个。

sentences.en: But his older brothers, Paul and Hank, they still let him in on a lot of the action.
sentences.zh: 但他的两个哥哥保罗和汉克，依然让他们的小弟参与进很多好玩的活动中。

sentences.en: We had a great childhood, especially for boys, because we were throwing rocks at each other, shooting bottle rockets at one another.
sentences.zh: 我们度过了美好的童年，对男孩子来说尤其如此，因为我们互相朝对方扔石头，朝彼此发射小火箭。

sentences.en: It was dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这很危险。

sentences.en: You know, boy stuff, throwing rocks at each other.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，男孩子气的东西，互相扔石头。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And just like that 80s movie that's probably playing in your head right now, Arlen could always hear his mom's voice in the distance when it was time to come running home again.
sentences.zh: 就像此刻可能正在你脑海中播放的那些80年代电影一样，每到该跑回家的时候，阿伦总能听到远处母亲的声音。

sentences.en: I could be half a mile away in the woods, and I could hear my mother's voice calling me.
sentences.zh: 我可以在半英里外的树林里，听到我母亲呼唤我的声音。

sentences.en: She would go out on the back deck and just yell.
sentences.zh: 她会走到后甲板上大声喊叫。

sentences.en: It was like a wild, animalistic mother calling her—trying to find her young out in the woods.
sentences.zh: 就像一只狂野的、充满母性的动物在呼唤——试图在树林里找到自己的幼崽。

sentences.en: As Arlen got older, he started to feel a need for a different kind of freedom.
sentences.zh: 随着阿伦渐渐长大，他开始感到需要一种不同类型的自由。

sentences.en: His parents were religious and conservative, and he felt like he didn't quite belong in their world, especially as he realized he was gay.
sentences.zh: 他的父母是宗教信徒且思想保守，他觉得自己并不完全属于他们的世界，特别是当他意识到自己是同性恋时。

sentences.en: So he decided to put some distance between himself and his hometown.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定和家乡保持一些距离。

sentences.en: I remember driving to college and playing my U2 cassette.
sentences.zh: 我记得开车去上大学时播放着U2乐队的磁带。

sentences.en: I remember seeing it at the top of my lungs.
sentences.zh: 我记得自己在大声唱着它。

sentences.en: I remember the roads were windy and taking those sharp curves just like, you know, with abandon.
sentences.zh: 我记得道路是盘山路，过那些急转弯时就那样，你知道的，无所顾忌。

sentences.en: And I think that was kind of the first moment I felt free.
sentences.zh: 我想那大概是我第一次感到自由的时刻。

sentences.en: Eventually, Arlen landed in California.
sentences.zh: 最终，阿伦在加利福尼亚落了脚。

sentences.en: He came out to his family, which in time they accepted.
sentences.zh: 他向家人出柜了，随着时间的推移，他们接受了这一点。

sentences.en: Then he got married and built a life on his own terMs.
sentences.zh: 然后他结婚了，按照自己的方式建立了自己的生活。

sentences.en: But even many years later, he still had lingering feelings about what it meant to be the son who left.
sentences.zh: 但即使在多年以后，对于当那个离开的儿子意味着什么，他心里依然有着挥之不去的感觉。

sentences.en: And he told me that when his mom started tracking his location, things got more complicated.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，当他的母亲开始追踪他的位置时，事情变得更加复杂了。

sentences.en: Arlen J.
sentences.zh: 阿伦·J·

sentences.en: Staggs, welcome to Modern Love.
sentences.zh: 斯塔格斯，欢迎来到《现代爱情》。

sentences.en: It is my pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很荣幸能来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: So, Arlen, after growing up in this tight-knit family in Alabama, you decide to leave the South and go live in California.
sentences.zh: 那么，阿伦，在阿拉巴马州这个紧密团结的家庭中长大后，你决定离开南方去加利福尼亚生活。

sentences.en: How did your mother feel about that?
sentences.zh: 你母亲对此有什么感觉？

sentences.en: She was devastated.
sentences.zh: 她心碎欲绝。

sentences.en: You know, my parents ended up teaching at the high school that they graduated from.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的父母最终在他们自己毕业的高中教书。

sentences.en: They lived in the same hometown their whole lives, which there's something very sweet about that.
sentences.zh: 他们一辈子都住在同一个家乡，这其中有一种非常温馨的感觉。

sentences.en: And I love that for them.
sentences.zh: 我为他们感到高兴。

sentences.en: But I think just California was so—I mean, in distance, yes, it's far.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得加州实在是——我是说，在距离上，是的，它很远。

sentences.en: But just in mindset and culture, it's so far away for them.
sentences.zh: 但在思维方式和文化上，对他们来说实在太遥远了。

sentences.en: Did you feel guilty for moving so far away?
sentences.zh: 你为搬到那么远的地方感到内疚吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In some ways, I still do.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我到现在还这么觉得。

sentences.en: It's almost like there's an agreement we all had, and I broke that agreement.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像我们之间曾有过一个协议，而我打破了这个协议。

sentences.en: Even though we never stated that agreement.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们从未明说那个协议。

sentences.en: Nobody would have never said—you know, we never sat down and said, okay, in this family, you're not allowed to move to California.
sentences.zh: 没有人会说——你知道的，我们从未坐在一起说过，好吧，在这个家族里，你不准搬去加州。

sentences.en: Does everybody agree?
sentences.zh: 大家同意吗？

sentences.en: But I knew I wasn't supposed to do that.
sentences.zh: 但我知道我不该那样做。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about how you first started sharing your location with your mom?
sentences.zh: 你能讲讲你是怎么开始和妈妈共享位置的吗？

sentences.en: Whose idea was it?
sentences.zh: 是谁的主意？

sentences.en: I remember it being her idea, but I was not resistant to it at all.
sentences.zh: 我记得那是她的主意，但我一点也不排斥。

sentences.en: So Drew is my husband.
sentences.zh: 德鲁是我的丈夫。

sentences.en: He and I had a vacation rental in Florida.
sentences.zh: 我和他在佛罗里达州有一套度假屋。

sentences.en: We lived in San Diego, but we would drive back and forth.
sentences.zh: 我们住在圣迭戈，但经常两地开车往返。

sentences.en: And the first time that we did it, my mom was like, you know, can you turn on your location on your phone so that we can see you?
sentences.zh: 第一次这么做的时候，我妈就说，你能不能在手机上打开定位，这样我们就能看到你在哪？

sentences.en: So I thought this is a great idea because if something did happen, somebody would know where we were.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这是个好主意，因为万一出什么事，别人能知道我们在哪。

sentences.en: And I think she found a lot of peace in kind of following our daily progress.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，通过关注我们的日常进展，她获得了很大的内心平静。

sentences.en: It was kind of fun for her to, you know, see how far we got each day.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，看看我们每天走了多远，其实也挺有意思的。

sentences.en: And it took about four days to drive across the country.
sentences.zh: 横穿全国开车大约需要四天时间。

sentences.en: She would be like, well, I see you're in Arkansas or it looks like you're getting close or you made really good time today or whatever.
sentences.zh: 她会说，嗯，我看到你在阿肯色州了，或者看起来你快到了，或者你今天赶路真快之类的。

sentences.en: But then at some point, location sharing with your mom started to become kind of a problem.
sentences.zh: 但后来在某个时候，和妈妈共享定位开始变成了一种负担。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what happened with that?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我讲讲后来怎么了吗？

sentences.en: I think when I started to notice that she would see me in a location and then make up a concern about it, then it became an issue.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，当我开始注意到她看到我的位置后，就会凭空捏造出一些担忧，这就成问题了。

sentences.en: So one time I took Chip, my dog, to the vet and my mom called later that day and she was like, is everything okay with Chip?
sentences.zh: 所以有一次我带我的狗奇普去兽医诊所，我妈那天晚些时候打电话来问，奇普没事吧？

sentences.en: And I was like, yes, he's fine.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，他很好。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Like, why are you asking that?
sentences.zh: 怎么突然这么问？

sentences.en: Do you know something?
sentences.zh: 你知道什么内情吗？

sentences.en: I don't know you.
sentences.zh: 我不认识你。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: She said, well, I just noticed that you were at the vet's office today and I worried that something bad happened.
sentences.zh: 她说，哦，我只是注意到你今天去了兽医诊所，我很担心是不是出了什么不好的事。

sentences.en: And by the way, nothing was wrong with him.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他一点事都没有。

sentences.en: It was literally just like an annual checkup.
sentences.zh: 真的就只是年度例行体检而已。

sentences.en: That was the first time I was like, okay, that's a little bit too invasive.
sentences.zh: 那是第一次我觉得，好吧，这有点太侵犯隐私了。

sentences.en: Stop watching me.
sentences.zh: 别盯着我了。

sentences.en: Like, you know, like it's none of your business that I'm at the vet.
sentences.zh: 就好像，我去兽医那儿跟你一点关系也没有。

sentences.en: And so I waited probably a few days and then just kind of once I knew she was had gone to bed and it was late in Alabama and maybe still early in California.
sentences.zh: 所以我大概等了几天，等我知道她已经上床睡觉了，当时阿拉巴马州已经很晚了，加州可能还早。

sentences.en: I just, you know, discreetly unshared my location.
sentences.zh: 我就悄悄地关闭了定位共享。

sentences.en: Did she notice?
sentences.zh: 她注意到了吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 注意到了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But it took her a while.
sentences.zh: 不过她花了点时间才发现。

sentences.en: I turned it off and maybe two or three weeks later, she was like, hey, I can't see your location anymore.
sentences.zh: 我关掉定位两三周后，她突然说，嘿，我看不到你的位置了。

sentences.en: You know, what happened?
sentences.zh: 怎么回事？

sentences.en: And so after that, I turned location sharing back on.
sentences.zh: 所以在那之后，我又把定位共享打开了。

sentences.en: And then one day I'm running errands.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天我正在外面办杂事。

sentences.en: My phone was in my pocket and I was unknowingly butt dialing her.
sentences.zh: 我的手机放在口袋里，在不知情的情况下误触拨号给她了。

sentences.en: And I did this probably seven or eight times, which, by the way, I'm very familiar with because since my name starts with A, this happens to me a lot.
sentences.zh: 我大概连续打了七八次，顺便说一句，我对这事太熟了，因为我的名字以A开头，这种事经常发生在我身上。

sentences.en: You're talking to Banana, my friend.
sentences.zh: 你在跟香蕉说话呢，我的朋友。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Do you get butt dialed a lot too?
sentences.zh: 你也很经常误触拨号吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: So, but for me, I don't ever assume the worSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，但对我和来说，我从来不会往最坏处想。

sentences.en: I just turn my phone off or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我只会把手机关机或者别的什么。

sentences.en: But when I got back in the car and I realized that she had, I think she had even maybe called back each time and she had texted me like, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 但当我回到车里，我意识到她甚至可能每次都回了电话，还给我发短信说，怎么回事？

sentences.en: And why do you keep calling me?
sentences.zh: 为什么你一直打电话给我？

sentences.en: And so I called her and she had made up this whole story about how she was afraid that I had been kidnapped and locked in a trunk.
sentences.zh: 所以我给她回了电话，她居然编造了整个故事，说她害怕我被绑架并锁在后备箱里。

sentences.en: Or maybe I was in a ditch somewhere and the only way I could communicate with her was like butt dialing for help.
sentences.zh: 或者我可能掉在哪条沟里了，唯一能和她沟通的方式就是通过误触拨号求救。

sentences.en: But she could see your location.
sentences.zh: 但她能看到你的位置啊。

sentences.en: Couldn't she see that you were in like a...
sentences.zh: 难道她看不出你在像……

sentences.en: She saw me in the Sam's Club.
sentences.zh: 她看到我在山姆会员店。

sentences.en: So I think she thought I was in the parking lot tied up in the trunk of a car.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜她以为我在停车场里，被五花大绑塞在汽车后备箱里。

sentences.en: I mean, you're laughing now, but it sounds like she was really scared.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你现在笑得出来，但听起来她当时真的吓坏了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know how committed she was to that interpretation, but that was the interpretation she had.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不知道她对这种解读有多笃定，但这确实是她的想法。

sentences.en: And it was clear to me at that point that she's really going to a dark place about it.
sentences.zh: 到那个时候我才明白，她真的把事情往很黑暗的方向想了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I don't know how much it serves her to know where I am.
sentences.zh: 我不知道让她知道我在哪到底有什么意义。

sentences.en: And after that, I turned location sharing back off.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我又把定位共享给关了。

sentences.en: Were you just turning on and off and on and off and on and off your location sharing for like years?
sentences.zh: 你是不是就这样开启、关闭、开启、关闭、开启、关闭定位共享持续了好几年？

sentences.en: Maybe for a year.
sentences.zh: 大概一年吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I usually blamed it on technology.
sentences.zh: 我通常把这归咎于科技。

sentences.en: That was my go-to scapegoat.
sentences.zh: 那是我的惯用借口。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 什么意思？

sentences.en: Is I would say, well, I would say, oh my gosh, my phone must have updated again or, you know, and it must have turned my location off.
sentences.zh: 我会说，天哪，我的手机肯定又自动更新了，或者你知道的，它肯定自动把我的定位关了。

sentences.en: Let me turn that back on for you.
sentences.zh: 我来帮你重新打开。

sentences.en: Like I would blame the iPhone.
sentences.zh: 就像我会怪苹果手机一样。

sentences.en: I would never say, yeah, well, I turned it off.
sentences.zh: 我绝对不会说，对啦，是我自己关的。

sentences.en: Because why?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？

sentences.en: This is one of those questions I have to think about because I don't know really.
sentences.zh: 这是我必须思考的问题之一，因为我其实也不知道。

sentences.en: I guess it felt easier to just keep going through the process of turning it off than having a conversation about it.
sentences.zh: 我想，比起坐下来好好谈谈，一遍又一遍地重复关闭定位的流程反而感觉更容易些。

sentences.en: It felt more efficient to press a button than to sit down and say, mom, let's talk about boundaries.
sentences.zh: 按一下按钮比坐下来对妈妈说“我们来谈谈边界感”要更有效率。

sentences.en: Let's talk about what's okay and what's not okay.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈什么可以做什么不可以。

sentences.en: And there's this history of, I left where I'm from.
sentences.zh: 而且我有一种背景，我离开了我的家乡。

sentences.en: I left home.
sentences.zh: 我离家出走了。

sentences.en: So I don't know if I just took on that like I was the bad son that didn't stay or it was never about her seeing me at the vet and getting upset about what might or might not have happened to Chip.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道自己是不是承担了那种角色——觉得自己是个没有留下来陪伴的坏儿子，或者这从来都不是关于她看到我在兽医那儿然后对奇普可能会或不会发生什么事感到心烦意乱。

sentences.en: It was always about this unresolved kind of broken agreement.
sentences.zh: 这始终是关于这种未解决的、破碎的某种默契。

sentences.en: That does not seem like something your mom was saying to you, right?
sentences.zh: 这听起来不像你妈对你说的话，对吧？

sentences.en: Like this was something you were saying to yourself.
sentences.zh: 这更像是你在对自己说的话。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So in addition to location sharing maybe not being so helpful for her anymore, it strikes me that it also was not so helpful for you, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，除了定位共享对她来说可能不再那么有用之外，我发现它对你其实也没有那么有用，对吧？

sentences.en: Like it's making you talk quite unkindly to yourself.
sentences.zh: 因为它让你对自己说了很多很不客气的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: But part of you, I really want to understand this, like part of you felt like you owed her this information about where you were?
sentences.zh: 但你内心深处——我真的很想理解这一点——你内心深处觉得你欠她这些关于你在哪的信息吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, a hundred percent.
sentences.zh: 是的，百分之百。

sentences.en: I felt like I owed it to her, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想我确实觉得我欠她的。

sentences.en: Especially after my brother Paul went missing.
sentences.zh: 特别是自我弟弟保罗失踪之后。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Arlen, can you tell me what happened with your brother Paul?
sentences.zh: 阿伦，你能跟我讲讲你弟弟保罗身上发生的事吗？

sentences.en: I guess the catalytic moment or the catalyst for all of it was when my mom got a phone call from the Alabaster, Alabama Police Department.
sentences.zh: 我想这一切的导火索或契机，是我妈妈接到了阿拉巴马州阿拉巴斯特警察局的电话。

sentences.en: And they had picked my brother up on Interstate 65.
sentences.zh: 他们在65号州际公路上把我弟弟带走了。

sentences.en: He had pretty extreme paranoia.
sentences.zh: 他有相当极端的妄想症。

sentences.en: He was hearing voices in his head.
sentences.zh: 他脑子里能听到声音。

sentences.en: And he was running from people that he claimed were trying to kill him.
sentences.zh: 而且他在躲避那些他声称想要杀他的人。

sentences.en: And, you know, this was a very shocking phone call to get because Paul had always been a little troubled.
sentences.zh: 你知道，接到这个电话非常令人震惊，因为保罗一直是个有点让人头疼的孩子。

sentences.en: And as a kid, I just remember him being grounded a lot and, you know, lots of teenage door slamming and loud 80s metal music playing from his room.
sentences.zh: 作为一个小男孩，我只记得他经常被罚禁足，你知道的，还有许多青少年摔门的声音，以及从他房间里传出来的响亮80年代重金属音乐。

sentences.en: And that just kind of continued through his life, you know, like he was just constantly unsettled.
sentences.zh: 这种状态贯穿了他的整个人生，你知道的，他总是处于一种心神不宁的状态。

sentences.en: But he was never at that level of, you know, a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 但他从来没有达到那种精神疾病的程度。

sentences.en: And so that was kind of the first moment that kind of, in a sense, woke us all up to like something deeply troubling is going on with Paul.
sentences.zh: 所以那是某种意义上的第一个时刻，它在某种程度上唤醒了我们所有人，让我们意识到保罗身上正在发生非常严重的问题。

sentences.en: Did you eventually find out what was happening with Paul?
sentences.zh: 你最后弄清楚保罗到底怎么了吗？

sentences.en: At the time, he was diagnosed with cannabis-induced psychosis.
sentences.zh: 当时，他被诊断为大麻诱发性精神病。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And what doesn't make sense about that to me is, from what I've read about that, is most cases, they can be that severe, but then it kind of goes away.
sentences.zh: 我觉得不可思议的是，根据我对此的了解，大多数病例虽然会很严重，但后来会逐渐消失。

sentences.en: It tapers off.
sentences.zh: 它会慢慢减弱。

sentences.en: And his did not.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有。

sentences.en: His continued and even got worse.
sentences.zh: 他的症状持续存在，甚至还恶化了。

sentences.en: When you say things got worse, can you share a little bit about what that means?
sentences.zh: 当你病情恶化时，能分享一下这意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: He, well, they got a little better in the beginning because he, they gave him some medication, which helped.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最开始情况有点好转，因为他们给他开了一些药，挺管用的。

sentences.en: And he lived with my parents for a while.
sentences.zh: 而且他在我父母家住了一段时间。

sentences.en: And the deal with my parents was, you know, they said, you can live in our home as long as you need to, but you have to take your medication.
sentences.zh: 和我父母的约定是，你知道的，他们说，只要你需要，你可以一直住在我们家，但你必须吃药。

sentences.en: And one day he just said, you know, I don't want to take it anymore.
sentences.zh: 有一天他突然说，你知道吗，我不想再吃了。

sentences.en: I'm going to leave.
sentences.zh: 我要离开。

sentences.en: And he did.
sentences.zh: 然后他真的走了。

sentences.en: And then what?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: Did you know where he was?
sentences.zh: 你知道他在哪里吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, we would get these calls.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们会接到这样的电话。

sentences.en: The first call that mom got was from Tallahassee and the authorities in Tallahassee had essentially rescued him from some kind of pond or swamp.
sentences.zh: 妈妈接到的第一个电话来自塔拉哈西，塔拉哈西的执法人员基本上把他从某种池塘或沼泽里救了上来。

sentences.en: I remember they mentioned that there were alligators in the body of water that he was in.
sentences.zh: 我记得他们提到他呆的水体里有短吻鳄。

sentences.en: And he always called the people that were trying to kill him, the goons.
sentences.zh: 他总是把那些试图杀他的人叫做“打手”。

sentences.en: And he was claiming that the goons had put poison on his skin.
sentences.zh: 他声称那些打手在他的皮肤上涂了毒药。

sentences.en: So he was in that water trying to wash the poison off of his skin.
sentences.zh: 所以他才泡在水里，想把皮肤上的毒药洗掉。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: And then they got a call from Tyler, Texas, and it was a psychiatric hospital.
sentences.zh: 然后他们接到了来自得克萨斯州泰勒市的电话，是一家精神病院打来的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the nurse had a conversation with my mom.
sentences.zh: 而且，护士和我妈进行了交谈。

sentences.en: And I remember mom said that her brother, like the nurse's brother, also had a similar condition.
sentences.zh: 我记得妈妈说她弟弟，也就是那个护士的弟弟，也有类似的情况。

sentences.en: And, you know, she was like, unless they take their meds, there's really nothing you can do.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，她说过，除非他们吃药，否则你真的无能为力。

sentences.en: And that was the last call that mom got, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想那是妈妈接到的最后一个电话。

sentences.en: What was it like not knowing where Paul was?
sentences.zh: 不知道保罗在哪里是什么感觉？

sentences.en: What was that like for you emotionally?
sentences.zh: 对你来说，那在情感上意味着什么？

sentences.en: I'd like to say that I had this deep concern for Paul, and I really wanted to go out and help Paul.
sentences.zh: 我很想说我对保罗有着深深的关切，我真的很想出去帮助保罗。

sentences.en: But I think Hank and I both became very protective of mom because she was worried about Paul enough for everybody.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我和汉克都变得非常保护妈妈，因为她为保罗操的心已经够所有人受的了。

sentences.en: And she would get lost in telling us all the specific details over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 她会陷入一遍又一遍地向我们讲述所有具体细节的死循环中。

sentences.en: And we would go all the way back to Alabaster, Alabama, and exactly what the police officer said on the phone, exactly what the receptionist at the hospital was wearing,
sentences.zh: 我们会一路回到阿拉巴马州阿拉巴斯特，复述警察在电话里到底说了什么，医院前台穿着什么样，

sentences.en: exactly what the muffin tasted like in the cafe where she bought a muffin.
sentences.zh: 她在买玛芬蛋糕的那家咖啡馆里吃的玛芬蛋糕是什么味道。

sentences.en: I think it was her way of saying, this is how we got here.
sentences.zh: 我想这是她的表达方式，意思是，我们就是这样走到这一步的。

sentences.en: And I need to make sense of how I lost my son.
sentences.zh: 我必须弄明白我是怎么失去儿子的。

sentences.en: Arlen, not too long after that, your family experiences a really sudden loss.
sentences.zh: 阿伦，在那不久之后，你的家庭经历了一次非常突然的变故。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what happened?
sentences.zh: 能告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: My dad went in for a heart procedure in 2022, and he was just going to have like a stent replaced.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸在2022年做了一个心脏手术，本来只是去更换一个支架。

sentences.en: It's supposed to be a very easy procedure.
sentences.zh: 这本该是一个非常简单的手术。

sentences.en: You know, they don't even use anesthesia.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们甚至不用麻醉。

sentences.en: But when they were done with the procedure, they fixed the stent, and he coded, and he didn't make it.
sentences.zh: 但当他们做完手术、修好支架后，他突发心脏骤停，没能挺过来。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 噢天哪，我太难过了。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: That is so much for your family to go through.
sentences.zh: 你的家庭经历的打击太大了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, I remember at dad's funeral, my brother Hank and I both gave a eulogy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得在爸爸的葬礼上，我和哥哥汉克都致了悼词。

sentences.en: I just remember stopping in the middle, and I asked the congregation if we could pray for Paul.
sentences.zh: 我只记得讲到一半时停了下来，请求会众为保罗祈祷。

sentences.en: And I prayed that God would show us where he is.
sentences.zh: 我祈求上帝让我们知道他在哪里。

sentences.en: And four months later, he was found dead in Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 四个月后，他在拉斯维加斯被发现已经身亡。

sentences.en: How did you find out about Paul's passing?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么得知保罗去世的消息的？

sentences.en: I got a call from the coroner's office in Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 我接到了拉斯维加斯法医办公室的电话。

sentences.en: Like, on Tuesday, I get the call.
sentences.zh: 周二那天，我接到了电话。

sentences.en: My mom's birthday is Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈的生日是周三。

sentences.en: And then Thanksgiving is on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 然后周四是感恩节。

sentences.en: My gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So I called Hank, and I said, we need to go and tell mom.
sentences.zh: 所以我给汉克打了电话，说我们需要去告诉妈妈。

sentences.en: I was in Florida at the time.
sentences.zh: 我当时在佛罗里达。

sentences.en: He was in Nashville.
sentences.zh: 他在纳什维尔。

sentences.en: So I get in the car.
sentences.zh: 于是我上了车。

sentences.en: We meet at my mom's house in Alabama.
sentences.zh: 我们在妈妈位于阿拉巴马州的房子碰面。

sentences.en: And, yeah, I remember turning on my location.
sentences.zh: 而且，对，我记得开启了手机定位。

sentences.en: Oh, you were doing the drive.
sentences.zh: 哦，你在开车。

sentences.en: You were doing the drive.
sentences.zh: 你当时在开车。

sentences.en: While I was doing the drive.
sentences.zh: 就在我开车的时候。

sentences.en: And we were going to have dinner with her, celebrate her birthday, and then tell her.
sentences.zh: 我们本来打算和她吃晚饭，庆祝她的生日，然后把这事告诉她。

sentences.en: And, yeah.
sentences.zh: 然后，对。

sentences.en: When you did tell her, what was that like?
sentences.zh: 当你真的告诉她时，那是什么样的感觉？

sentences.en: I don't have the word for it.
sentences.zh: 我无法用言语来形容。

sentences.en: But when Dad passed away, it was what I would call a very pure grief.
sentences.zh: 但爸爸去世时，那是我所说的非常纯粹的悲伤。

sentences.en: Like when we say grief, what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 就像我们说悲伤时，所指的那种感觉。

sentences.en: When Paul passed, there was definitely grief.
sentences.zh: 保罗去世时，当然也有悲伤。

sentences.en: But it was mixed with relief and closure.
sentences.zh: 但其中夹杂着如释重负和尘埃落定的感觉。

sentences.en: And you knew where he was.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道他在哪里。

sentences.en: We knew where he was.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他在哪里。

sentences.en: And I remember both of us just holding her.
sentences.zh: 我记得我们两个人都紧紧抱着她。

sentences.en: She just cried and cried and cried for what felt like a really long time.
sentences.zh: 她只是不停地哭啊哭啊，感觉哭了很长很长的时间。

sentences.en: And I remember I was, the position of my body was so uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时我身体的姿势非常不舒服。

sentences.en: My leg was falling asleep.
sentences.zh: 我的腿都麻了。

sentences.en: And my back was starting to hurt.
sentences.zh: 我的背也开始痛起来。

sentences.en: And, but I could not break that blob that we made by hugging her.
sentences.zh: 但是，我无法打破我们抱著她时围成的那团“肉球”。

sentences.en: What a word.
sentences.zh: 这词用得真好。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就是，对。

sentences.en: In a blob.
sentences.zh: 像个肉球一样。

sentences.en: You said when you were driving back home to tell your mother about Paul's passing, you turned your location back on.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说，当你开车回家准备把保罗去世的消息告诉母亲时，你重新打开了定位。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Did you ever turn it off again?
sentences.zh: 你后来又把它关掉过吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe I had gone on one of my trips to reflect and grieve and pray.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许我曾去进行过一次次旅行，去反思、悲伤和祈祷。

sentences.en: And I don't know what prompted me to turn it off.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是什么促使我把它关掉的。

sentences.en: But at some point, I did turn it off again.
sentences.zh: 但不知在什么时候，我又把它关掉了。

sentences.en: And then a few months later, Mom comes to visit me in Florida.
sentences.zh: 然后几个月后，妈妈来佛罗里达看望我。

sentences.en: And I was taking her back after her visit to the airport.
sentences.zh: 在她访问结束后，我开车送她去机场。

sentences.en: And then I come in and I kind of walk her to the TSA line.
sentences.zh: 我送她进去，陪她走到安检排队的地方。

sentences.en: And I remember I hugged her, said goodbye.
sentences.zh: 我记得我拥抱了她，向她道别。

sentences.en: I love you.
sentences.zh: 我爱你。

sentences.en: I'm just kind of standing there watching her.
sentences.zh: 我只是站在那里看着她。

sentences.en: And she hands her ID to the officer.
sentences.zh: 她把身份证递给安检人员。

sentences.en: She starts to put her bag up on the machine.
sentences.zh: 她开始把包放到安检机器上。

sentences.en: And the sadness overwhelmed me.
sentences.zh: 悲伤瞬间涌上心头。

sentences.en: That scene of her doing all those things all by herself, I just felt like somebody should be getting on that plane with her.
sentences.zh: 看到她一个人做所有这些事情的场景，我只觉得应该有人陪她一起上飞机。

sentences.en: Somebody should be putting her carry-on in the overhead bin for her.
sentences.zh: 应该有人帮她把随身行李放到头顶的行李舱里。

sentences.en: Somebody should be there with her.
sentences.zh: 应该有人陪伴在她身边。

sentences.en: She's just kind of always been surrounded by these strong men.
sentences.zh: 她一直以来身边都围绕着这些坚强的男人们。

sentences.en: And now she's doing all this by herself.
sentences.zh: 而现在她得独自面对这一切。

sentences.en: And by the way, not to—she's an incredibly strong woman.
sentences.zh: 而且顺便说一句，并不是要——她本身就是个极其坚强的女人。

sentences.en: Of course, of course, of course, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，当然，当然，当然。

sentences.en: Not to invalidate her at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是想否定她。

sentences.en: And she wasn't falling apart.
sentences.zh: 而且她没有崩溃。

sentences.en: I was.
sentences.zh: 崩溃的是我。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And then, you know, what's there underneath it all is just all the years that I had run away to California.
sentences.zh: 然后呢，你知道的，这一切深层埋藏着的，其实是我逃往加州的那些年。

sentences.en: And all the years that I wasn't there and the birthdays where I just called and sent flowers and I wasn't there for the party,
sentences.zh: 以及我不在身边的那些年，那些我只能打电话、送鲜花而没能出席派对的生日，

sentences.en: I went back to my car and just sort of allowed myself to cry.
sentences.zh: 我回到车里，终于忍不住哭了起来。

sentences.en: To cry about dad, to cry about Paul, to cry about her.
sentences.zh: 为爸爸哭泣，为保罗哭泣，为她哭泣。

sentences.en: And that was the moment when I'm sitting there in my car in the airport parking lot where I needed to share my location with her.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，我坐在机场停车场的车里，我意识到我需要跟她共享我的位置。

sentences.en: Like, I needed it.
sentences.zh: 真的，我太需要了。

sentences.en: And I almost felt like—it was almost like being a little boy again.
sentences.zh: 我甚至觉得——那种感觉就像是回到了小时候。

sentences.en: Like, there I was lost in the woods and I'm going to say, here I am.
sentences.zh: 就像我在树林里迷了路，然后我要说，我在这儿。

sentences.en: And you don't ever have to wonder where I am.
sentences.zh: 从此你再也不用猜我在哪里了。

sentences.en: And that's when it started to give me peace to know that she could get peace by looking at that.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，我知道她只要看一眼就能安心，这反而让我内心平静了下来。

sentences.en: You know, Arlen, it's interesting you say that because we've been talking all this time about location sharing, but it strikes me that, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，阿伦，你这么说很有意思，因为我们聊了这么久的位置共享，但我突然觉得，你知道的，

sentences.en: really what we're talking about is your family relationships, right?
sentences.zh: 其实我们谈论的是你的家庭关系，对吧？

sentences.en: Your complicated, joyful, devastating, beautiful family relationships.
sentences.zh: 你那复杂、充满欢乐、令人心碎又美丽的家庭关系。

sentences.en: I mean, it's—
sentences.zh: 我是说，这——

sentences.en: Yeah, and we're also talking about this dance between boundaries and grief and how the two interact.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我们也在探讨界限与悲伤之间的这种拉扯，以及它们是如何相互影响的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, because it was the grief that had the boundary fall away.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为正是悲伤让那道界限消融了。

sentences.en: And I think it's almost—like, I think the simplest example of that is it would be really weird for me to pass you on the street, Anna, and then just grab you and hug you.
sentences.zh: 我想这几乎——最简单的例子就是，安娜，如果我在街上遇到你，然后突然冲过去抱住你，这会显得非常奇怪。

sentences.en: But if I were to pass you on the street and I know you just lost your dog,
sentences.zh: 但如果我在街上遇到你，而我知道你刚失去了爱犬，

sentences.en: it would not be weird for me to grab you and hug you because you're—because the grief changes that boundary.
sentences.zh: 我冲过去抱住你就一点也不奇怪，因为你——因为悲伤改变了那道界限。

sentences.en: And I think maybe that's what we're having a conversation about.
sentences.zh: 我想这也许才是我们真正在探讨的话题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's just so much more than toggling a little switch.
sentences.zh: 这远不仅仅是拨一下开关那么简单。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It definitely feels like an act of love.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一种爱的行为。

sentences.en: Arlen J.
sentences.zh: 阿伦·J·

sentences.en: Staggs, thank you so much for this conversation today.
sentences.zh: 斯塔格斯，非常感谢你今天接受我们的访谈。

sentences.en: It's been my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: I've loved it.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢这次聊聊。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎进了一群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党便陷入了一场残酷、混乱且有时令人心潮澎湃的权力斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》播客中，我和萨拉·科尼格将为你讲述那些试图维持影响力却在过程中渐渐失控的人的故事。
